Step 1

Read the labels

+
+

Each value on the other screens carries one of these three labels. The label says who produced the value. Read it before you weigh the value.

+
+
generateda hook or render-trace.mjs wrote it, never an agent producing the code

The compiled-at stamp in the header above is generated.

+
recordeda hook stored an agent's judgement verbatim; the agent can't alter it afterwards

A reviewer or security verdict is recorded: you read the agent's own words, not a summary of them.

+
writtenby David or the main session

Text authored by a person or the main session carries this label. Read it as a claim made by its author, not as a measurement.

+
+
+
+
+ +
+
+

Step 2

Look up the terms

+
+

A status is always a word, a glyph and a colour. Colour is never the only signal.

+
+
Pass

What was counted or checked passed. A count says what it was counted from.

+
Fail

A recorded check or verdict failed. It keeps its own rung and is never folded into a count.

+
Warn

A gap or disagreement in the trail. Read the sentence beside it before relying on the value.

+
Pending

Not done yet, so there is nothing to check yet.

+
Not built

Not built yet. There is no red, green, refactor, QA step or sign-off to show, and the page says so instead of inventing one.

+
+

Terms used on the other screens.

  • Rung. One numbered step in a story. The number is the step's position in the order, not a time.
  • Red, green, refactor. The values of a commit's TDD trailer. A rule page puts the red commit above the green one, so you read the order from position.
  • Attempt. One pass of a node through the build loop. Every attempt keeps its own rung; retries are never folded into a counter.
  • gate.stub. A recorded check, shown with what it expected and what it returned.
  • Verdict. A reviewer's or security agent's PASS or FAIL, recorded verbatim.
  • Finding. A problem a verdict raised. A later commit's Fixes-Finding trailer names the one it fixes.
  • Human decision. A point where David approved, steered or merged. They are listed together on the Human decisions screen.
  • Git-only. A node with no trail files; what is shown comes from git alone.
  • Snapshot. The commit this site was compiled from, stamped in step 5.

    I1FixedTestable

    Symptom
    four SELL-1 accept tests pass on the canned stub. They are New_reference_is_sold_with_201_and_its_Location_and_reads_back (SellReferenceTests.cs:22-29), Policy_sold_reads_back_by_its_reference_in_lower_case (:44-53), Reference_of_3_characters_is_accepted (:99-104) and Reference_of_20_characters_is_accepted (:120-127).
    Cause
    these tests check nothing beyond the shared helper SellAndReadBack (PoliciesClient.cs:43-55). The helper checks 201 (:46), that Location equals /policies/{expected} (:48), GET 200 (:51), and that the read-back reference equals the expected one (:53). The stub can meet every one of those checks with no storage. It builds Location from the request's own reference (PoliciesController.cs:16-17), and the GET builds the body's reference from the route (PoliciesController.cs:21-22, 24-25). So the reference read back is just the route echoed back. The extra asserts at :28 and :52 repeat that echo. The lower-case test does not show that a case-insensitive lookup found the stored row, because the stub upper-cases the route itself (PoliciesController.cs:22). Reference_is_trimmed_and_upper_cased_in_the_Location_and_the_stored_policy (:33-40) has the same weakness. It is red today only because the DTO pattern at SellPolicyRequest.cs:22 rejects surrounding spaces before any trimming, so it gets a 400. Once green fixes that, an echoing stub would pass it too. Rule: 'The client supplies the reference. It is trimmed and upper-cased, then must match ^[A-Z0-9-]{3,20}$ … abc-1 and ABC-1 are the same policy.' Accepted means stored and readable as sold, and these tests never check that.

    I1FixedTestable

    Symptom
    live POST /policies/{ref}/claims returns 500 with an InvalidOperationException saying RecordClaimRequest has validation metadata on record property 'Description' that will be ignored.
    Cause
    CancellationContracts.cs:38-40 declares RecordClaimRequest as a positional record and targets its DataAnnotations at the generated properties ('[property: Required] DateOnly? ClaimDate' at :39 and '[property: MaxLength(500)] string? Description' at :40). MVC builds a positional record through its primary constructor, so it reads validation metadata from the constructor parameters. When it finds validators on a property that maps to a constructor parameter, it throws during object-model validation instead of quietly ignoring them. The throw happens on every request whose body deserialises into a RecordClaimRequest (PoliciesController.cs:63 binds it from the body), so the happy path, 404, 422 and DataAnnotations-400 cases all become 500s. +# inv-007: U3 review fails on values the kit can't draw and a fixed provenance sentence
+## Question
+Why does U3's screen layer render a recorded P0 verdict finding as P2 at attempt 2, and is the cause in the kit's VerdictCard severity type or in the screen?
+## Hypothesis
+The kit's VerdictCard types severity as 'P1' | 'P2', so the screens coerce P0 to P2. The reviewer's other three
+findings (a fixed "recorded by the orchestrator" sentence, an ok-less gate drawn as waived, a null testable drawn as
+Untestable) are screen mappings that turn a missing or differing value into a claim, and no fixture holds any of
+these values. Disproved by VerdictCard accepting P0, or by a fixture already holding one of these cases.
+## Evidence
+- docs/trace/ui/U3/verdicts/A2-reviewer.json: FAIL, R1 P1 (LOOP-3), R2-R4 P2; A2-security.json: PASS, S1 P2
+- docs/trace/ui/U3/findings/A2.md: the investigator's diagnosis, I1-I5
+- src/web/kit/project/verdict-card/VerdictCard.tsx:14, :164: severity 'P1' | 'P2', tone knows only P1;
+  src/web/app/explorer/verdict/Verdict.tsx:116 and Ladder.tsx:85 write `severity === 'P1' ? 'P1' : 'P2'`
+- docs/ui/components.md:89, :91, :92: the gate-row, verdict-card and finding-card rows list no P0, no
+  "ok not recorded" and no "testable not recorded" state
+- src/web/app/explorer/loop/Loop.tsx:42-43: the provenance sentence is a constant; 37 real loop lines carry
+  source 'reconciled'; the signed-off node reference words it "per its source field"
+- tests/web/fixtures/trails/**: every severity P1 or P2, every loop line source orchestrator, every gate line has ok,
+  every finding has a boolean testable
+## Findings
+**Yes: the cause of R1 is in the kit** (VerdictCard can't say P0), with a screen coercion on top. Of the other
+three, R2 is in the screen alone; R3 and R4 are kit gaps too, which disproves that part of the hypothesis.
+Diagnosis in [findings/A2.md](../../trace/ui/U3/findings/A2.md).
+- I1 (R1, LOOP-3) · kit plus screen: VerdictCard.tsx:14 has no P0; Verdict.tsx:116, Ladder.tsx:85 coerce it to P2,
+  and Verdict.tsx:45 tones a P0 like a P2. No recorded verdict file holds a P0 today. New.
+- I2 (R2, DATA-2) · screen: Loop.tsx:42-43 asserts one source for every log; 37 reconciled lines exist in real
+  trails, U3's own among them. New.
+- I3 (R3, LOOP-1) · kit plus screen: GateRow's results (GateRow.tsx:13) are all claims; Ladder.tsx:19 maps ok null

+# p0-reconciled
+
+`retry-ladder` (see its README) with two values that fixture never holds, each one the case behind a U3 finding of
+round A2. Everything else (`base/`, `commits.json`, `files/`, the activity log, the findings rounds, the other three
+verdicts) is a byte-for-byte copy of `retry-ladder`, so every fact in that README holds here unless this one says otherwise.
+
+- **A P0 verdict finding** (U3 A2/I1, LOOP-3): in `verdicts/A2-reviewer.json`, **R1** has severity **P0** where
+  `retry-ladder` has P1. The verdict schema allows P0 (P0: the rule or acceptance is broken). R2 stays P2. Loop line
+  12, the A2 reviewer verdict event, gives R1 as P0 in its detail. The verdict page and attempt 2's verdict step on
+  the loop ladder must both draw R1 as **P0**, never as P2, with a tone at least as severe as P1's.
+- **A reconciled loop line** (U3 A2/I2, DATA-2): loop line **13**, inserted after the A2 verdicts and before the
+  `attempt++` to 3, has `source` **`reconciled`** and every other line has `source` `orchestrator`. It is cut from
+  the real `build/F0b` shape (`reconciled(activity.jsonl)`, no head, detail `redactCommand re-applied: 0 of 7
+  command records changed`, 7 being the activity records before its time). Its event is neither a gate nor a state,
+  so the gate timeline doesn't list it. The loop page's source sentence must name line 13 as reconciled and must not
+  say every event was recorded by the orchestrator.
+
+Inserting line 13 moves `retry-ladder`'s lines 13 to 23 down by one: attempt 3 runs from `attempt++` at line 14 to
+`gate.integrate` at line 24. The gate and state events, as `<attempt>·<line> <event>`, are: 1·2
+`state(in_progress)`, 1·3 `gate.red`, 1·4 `gate.stub` (ok false), 2·7 `gate.finding-red`, 2·8 `gate.stub`, 2·10
+`gate.green`, 3·16 `state(investigating)`, 3·18 `state(in_progress)`, 3·19 `gate.finding-red`, 3·20 `gate.green`,
+3·23 `gate.qa`, 3·24 `gate.integrate`.

+part of a trail, and a severity is not checked.

+(`retry-ladder` and `p0-reconciled`, `tests/web/fixtures/trails/`), so the live trail doesn't affect it. Filter by the
+path `e2e/U3/`: a bare `U3/` also matches the worktree's folder, `ui-U3/`, and runs every spec.
+
+```sh
+DOCKET_APP_PORT=4174 npm --prefix src/web run e2e -- e2e/U3/ --grep "LOOP-1 · "    # one rule's acceptance tests
+npm --prefix src/web run test -- -t "LOOP-1 · "                                   # one rule's unit tests
+```
+
+When you finish, run `rm -r src/web/public src/web/test-results`. Neither folder is git-ignored (note 8), so never
+stage them.
+
+## Console snippets
+
+Paste these into the DevTools Console on the page the step names. The steps refer to them by S-number.
+
+```js
+// S1: the gate timeline: how many rows, the rows by result, and the rows drawn as failed.
+rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-region="gate-timeline"] [data-kind]')];
+c = {}; rows.forEach((r) => { const k = r.dataset.result ?? 'state'; c[k] = (c[k] ?? 0) + 1; });
+[rows.length, JSON.stringify(c), rows.filter((r) => r.dataset.result === 'failed').map((r) => r.getAttribute('aria-label')).join('; ')]
+
+// S2: the loop page's steps per attempt, as marker(stage). On the loop page only: the node page keeps them behind a control.
+[1, 2, 3].map((n) => [...(document.querySelector(`ol[aria-label="Steps of attempt ${n}"]`)?.children ?? [])].map((li) => `${li.firstElementChild.textContent}(${li.dataset.stage})`).join(' '))
+
+// S3: the ladder's verdict steps that say their file is missing.
+[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-region="attempt-ladder"] p')].map((p) => p.textContent).filter((t) => t.endsWith('the verdict file is not in the trail.'))
+
+// S4: how far the page scrolls sideways (0: it doesn't).
+document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth
+
+// S5: the provenance labels on the page, in page order.
+[...document.querySelectorAll('main [data-provenance]')].map((e) => e.dataset.provenance).join(', ')
+```

+## Notes
+
+1. **A fix commit is found only for a round named `A<n>` (steps 38 and 39).** `compiler/index.ts:289` matches a
+   finding to a commit only when the trailer reads `A<n>/<id>`. `fixesFinding` (`:72`) parses only `/^A(\d+)\//`, so
+   three kinds of trailer never match. A steer round's `D2/I3` doesn't. A re-review round's `A3.2/I1` or `A2.4/I1`
+   doesn't either. And a bare `I2` keeps no round. At ca3f1a3, ten rounds read `No fix commit recorded` for every
+   finding, 44 findings in all: build/F1 D1 and D2, F6 D1, F0b D1, ui/U0b D1, U1 D1, D2 and D3, build/F5 A2.4 and
+   ui/W1 A3.2. That includes findings a commit names exactly. The fixture's rounds are A1 to A3 only. Step 39 is a
+   failure. The bare ids (step 38) are your ruling, because `I2` alone doesn't say which round it means. The
+   trace-data skill names `compiler/aliases.ts` as the home for `Fixes-Finding` forms, and that file doesn't exist.
+2. **On a ui node, each attempt's turn line sits one rung early (step 19).** `Ladder.tsx` takes the turn under rung
+   n from the `attempt++` event whose attempt is n + 1. The build logs write `attempt++` with the attempt it starts:
+   F2's line 5 is attempt 2, `1 → 2 …`. Every ui log writes it with the attempt it ends: U3's lines 5 and 33 are
+   attempts 1 and 2, and U0b, U1, U2 and W1 do the same. So on every ui node, a rung shows the next attempt's turn, the
+   last rung before the end shows none, and the first turn line isn't shown anywhere. The fix could match each turn by
+   its position in the log, between rung n's last event and rung n + 1's first. Or the log convention could be made
+   one. Choosing between them is part of the fix.
+3. **U0b's ladder says six verdict files are missing when they're in the trail (step 20).** U0b's loop lines 78, 79,
+   101, 102, 129 and 130 name their files relative to the node, as `verdicts/A4-security.json`. `verdictStep` looks
+   the file up by exact match against the compiled path, `docs/trace/ui/U0b/verdicts/A4-security.json`, so it finds
+   nothing. It then says `the verdict file is not in the trail`, which is false: the verdict pages render those files.
+   That breaks HONEST-1. F0b's three misses are real.
+4. **A finding's text is lost or misfiled when its markers vary (steps 35, 36 and 40).** `splitRootCause`
+   (`compiler/plans.ts:232`) knows only `Symptom:`, `Cause:` and `Fix direction:`. A variant such as `Cause
+   (classification: code):` or `Cause (kit):` isn't a marker, so the cause runs on inside Symptom. The Cause row then
+   says `no "Cause:" marker in the recorded text`, which the text beside it contradicts. Text before the first marker
+   is dropped. When the only marker is `Fix direction:`, the symptom and cause are both dropped, and the page shows
+   none of the recorded root cause. That happens for 18 of the 135 real findings, among them build/F2 A1/I2, F1b
+   A1/I2, F3 A1/I2, F6 A1/I1 to I5, ui/U1 A1/I2 and W1 A2/I1 to I6. In all, 33 cards show the Cause gap. Every
+   fixture finding uses the three exact markers.
+5. **The loop page scrolls sideways at 390 (step 23).** In a ladder step, the kit verdict card's rule chips
+   (`kit-verdict-card__chips`) don't wrap. A security verdict covers about ten IDs, and that row is wider than the
+   step. On the verdict page the card has the full width and wraps (step 49). RESP-1 is a SHOULD, and this is a kit
+   fix (`/kit-gap`, verdict-card) or a U7 line. The fixture's security verdict covers short IDs, so the U3 width tests
+   don't see it.
+6. **A rung's tag is its first ok-false gate, and a commit follows the gate that ran at it (steps 14, 21 and 22).**
+   `outcomeOf` tags an attempt with its first gate that came back ok false, and only falls back to its verdicts when
+   no gate failed. So W1's attempt 4 reads `Failed at gate.integrate`, though W1 passed review and was signed off in
+   it. U2's attempt 2 reads `Failed at gate.e2e-regression`, a change ruled intended. U3's attempts 2 and 3 read the
+   same, whatever the A3 verdicts say. The loop's question is "which gate failed, and did the attempt after it pass the
+   same gate?". The tag answers the first half, but it reads as how the attempt ended. Separately, a fixing commit is
+   placed after the event whose head it is. A gate then sits above the commit it checked, as with F2's #30 under 3·28.
+   Both are your ruling: keep as built, or tag by how the attempt ended and place a commit before its gate.
+7. **Loop events and the ladder's verdict cards show no provenance label (step 47).** trace.json gives every event
+   `provenance: generated` and every verdict and finding `recorded`. DATA-2 says "the UI shows the label wherever the
+   item appears". The verdict and finding pages show `recorded`. The loop page and the node page's Attempts show
+   events and verdict cards with no label, only the source sentence. The source sentence gives the log's own `source`
+   field (orchestrator or reconciled), which is not one of DATA-2's three labels. The signed-off loop screen has no

+How the finding page reads a recorded `root_cause` at f8c3471 (LOOP-4): the text splits at `Symptom:`, `Cause:` and
+`Fix direction:`, and a marker may carry a qualifier in brackets, as in `Cause (kit):`. A marker counts only at the start
+of the text, or after `.`, `!` or `?` and a space, or after a new line. It doesn't count inside double quotes, backticks
+or curly quotes. Text before the first marker opens the Symptom. A repeated marker's text joins its field, in order. A
+qualifier stays at the front of its field's text, without its colon, for example `(kit) VerdictFinding.severity …`.
+Only the marker words themselves are dropped. A field with no marker reads `no "<name>:" marker in the recorded text`.
+Text with no marker at all is kept whole as the Cause.
